description: I’m a student interested in biology, mathematics, astronomy, and technology. I enjoy exploring scientific concepts and applying them to real-world challenges. For this challenge, I’m developing health-monitoring software designed to track astronauts’ health during space missions. I’m particularly interested in the intersection of human biology and space exploration, and I’m excited to develop my idea while gaining experience in applying technology to challenges beyond Earth.
summary:
Orbital Vigilance is an interactive astronaut health-monitoring prototype designed to explore early signs of physical and cognitive fatigue during space missions.

Spaceflight can disrupt sleep, affect cardiovascular health, and reduce physical performance, putting astronaut well-being and mission safety at risk.

Our project investigates how combining heart rate variability (HRV), reaction time, physical performance, and sleep data could help identify concerning health patterns earlier. Through interactive simulations, visualizations, and NASA-supported research, users can explore how these measurements relate to one another.

Orbital Vigilance aims to support the future of proactive astronaut health monitoring, helping researchers explore ways to recognize potential fatigue before it compromises performance and mission safety.
details:
Orbital Vigilance is an interactive astronaut health-monitoring prototype designed to explore early signs of physical and cognitive fatigue during space missions.

Our project investigates how combining heart rate variability (HRV), reaction time, physical performance, and sleep patterns could help identify concerning health changes before they significantly affect an astronaut’s performance.

The website features an interactive health dashboard, simulated astronaut data, and visual graphs that allow users to compare measurements over time. It also includes an interactive investigation tool, ECG demonstrations, reaction-time testing, and explanations of how NASA monitors astronaut health.

We developed the project using Base44, an AI-powered website development platform, supported by NASA research and publicly available scientific information. This allowed us to create a functional, interactive prototype without building the entire application manually.

What makes Orbital Vigilance unique is its focus on connecting multiple health indicators rather than examining each one separately. We considered scientific accuracy, individual health differences, microgravity’s effects, and the importance of avoiding false warnings. All simulated data is clearly labeled, and the prototype does not claim to provide medical diagnoses.

Our goal is to demonstrate how integrated health monitoring could contribute to earlier fatigue detection, better-informed health assessments, and improved astronaut safety during long-duration space missions.
